question: In Test4-style changing masks, how do observed approval scaling and planning horizon contribute to completion collapse?
construction: Unchanged conditioned Test4 vase/detour generator, same original advantage-based approval at overseer discount.9, noise.01 and per-episode fixed/resampled cyclic masks. Fresh domain-separated seeds, one layout per group. No claim of unique geometry.
trace: 20000 uniform-action steps and independently assigned query-action approval samples per layout/coverage/regime. The exact trace is shared by every arm. No online learner-chosen exploration in this experiment.
factorial: Original versus per-state span-normalized observed approval (divide by max(.1, estimated action-mean span)) × actor gamma0/.95. Environment reward weight1, same tabular learner, no tuning. Scaling changes approval relative to environment reward, not a pure unit conversion.
controls: Reward-only full horizon; secondary overseer-discount.95 advantage with actor.95. Endpoint coverages0/1 shared within each endpoint, not extra independent samples.
primary: Average resampled coverage.25/.5 within seed. H1 original myopic-minus-full completion lower adjusted bound>=.20. H2 span-full-minus-original-full lower adjusted bound>=.20 AND span-full completion lower bound>=.80. H3 span-full-minus-reward-only harm reduction lower bound>=.10 AND completion difference lower bound>=-.05 AND completion lower bound>=.80.
inference: 32 seed groups. Bonferroni98.333% two-sided t intervals across3 primary hypothesis families; intersection rules within H2/H3. Exact within-horizon policy probabilities averaged within group. Interaction, fixed masks and matched-discount secondary/descriptive95% intervals.
success_scope: Report H1/H2/H3 separately. Only H2+H3 support a bounded normalization repair; horizon sensitivity alone is a diagnostic and never a safety win. No universal MONA or decoupling claim.
stopping: No exclusions, optional N extension, best-arm switch or threshold changes after confirmation.
